_doc: Category-32 (Condiments, Sauces and Dressings) compiler config for tools/standards/compile-cat32.mjs — HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default). Numbers come ONLY from data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv, selected per subcategory by explicit scope regex, strictest across jurisdictions, at FACE VALUE. Vinegar and tomato condiments have direct sovereign scopes (Vietnam QCVN 8-2 vinegar; Paraguay/MERCOSUR tomato concentrates; Singapore Food Regs ketchup). Soy sauce, fish sauce and mustard/mayo/dressings have NO direct sovereign ML and resolve by disclosed read-across from the nearest sovereign analog: Singapore 'tomato ketchup and other sauces' for the terrestrial condiment sauces; fish-muscle MLs for fish sauce (a fermented marine product); EU fruiting-vegetable nickel for tomato condiments. FISH SAUCE is the marine case: methylmercury IS material (aquatic methylation pathway) and is read across from the fish MeHg ML (Mexico NOM-242 500), then reconciled against the total-mercury read-across (EU lower-mercury fish 300) — where MeHg is not below tHg it is subsumed. No occurrence percentiles anywhere; every unregulated cell is a disclosed read-across, a control (reflex screen where a pathway exists), or a rebuttable not-material determination tested against the register each build.

vinegar.name: Vinegar (distilled, wine, balsamic, cider, rice)
vinegar.lineage_note: Vietnam QCVN 8-2 is the only sovereign that sets vinegar MLs (Pb 500, Cd 1000, tAs 200, tHg 50), so it governs directly. Hidden-hazard flag for the ratchet, NOT a missing limit: the FDA has issued balsamic- and wine-vinegar lead warning letters (grape-derived lead concentrated during must reduction, compounded historically by lead-bearing equipment), and measured balsamic lead can approach or exceed 500 ug/kg — so ALARA and the occurrence ratchet drive tightening after publication even though the sovereign ceiling is the correct initial value. Nickel and total chromium are held under a stainless-steel-migration screen because an acidic food in prolonged stainless contact leaches both.

iAs.rationale: No sovereign inorganic-arsenic ML exists for vinegar; total arsenic is governed (200, Vietnam). Inorganic arsenic is the toxic species, obtained by reflex speciation on any elevated total arsenic.
iAs.reference_method: Total As by ICP-MS; reflex iAs speciation (HPLC-ICP-MS) on any total-As exceedance.

MeHg.rationale: Vinegar is a fermented fruit- or grain-derived acid with no aquatic methylation pathway and no fish source. Total mercury is governed (50, Vietnam).

The source instrument writes the drinking-water chromium ceiling on the hexavalent species; it is adopted here as the total-chromium ceiling and disclosed as such, with the hexavalent fraction bound more tightly in the Cr-VI cell. Disclosed species-as-total ceiling: the anchor is a hexavalent-chromium limit applied as the ceiling for total chromium, which is at least as protective (total Cr ≤ the Cr-VI limit bounds Cr-VI as well); no sovereign sets a total-chromium level for this product on its basis.

fish-sauce.name: Fish sauce (fermented anchovy/marine sauce)
fish-sauce.lineage_note: No sovereign sets a fish-sauce ML. Fish sauce is a fermented marine product (anchovy hydrolysate), so every metal reads across from the fish-muscle sovereign MLs of the marine source: Pb 300 (EU muscle meat of fish), Cd 50 (Costa Rica fish in general), tAs 2000 (AU-NZ fish), iAs 100 (EU 2025/1891 muscle meat of fish), tHg 300 (EU lower-mercury fish). The generic Vietnam 'Sauce' MLs (tHg 50 etc.) are deliberately NOT applied: fish sauce is a marine fermentate whose contaminant profile follows its fish source, not the condiment-sauce category — and Vietnam, the world's largest fish-sauce producer, does not cap nuoc mam mercury at the generic-sauce 50 (anchovy-based fish sauce routinely exceeds it), which confirms nuoc mam sits outside that category. The generic-sauce values are retained in the audit trail as a different product form. Methylmercury IS material here — the aquatic methylation pathway is the whole point of a marine read-across — and is read across from the fish MeHg ML (Mexico NOM-242 500); it is then reconciled against total mercury, and because 500 is not below the 300 total-mercury ceiling it is subsumed (bounded by tHg, enforced by reflex speciation). Inorganic arsenic (100) is published alongside total arsenic (2000) because it is a strictly tighter toxic-species control: arsenic in fish is high but predominantly organic (arsenobetaine).

Pb.label: read-across from EU 2023/915 muscle meat of fish Pb 300 — fish sauce is a marine (fish-derived) product; the fish-muscle lead ML is the source-appropriate sovereign value.

Cd.label: read-across from Costa Rica RTCR 409 'fish in general' Cd 50 — the strictest sovereign fish-muscle cadmium ML.

tAs.label: read-across from AU-NZ Standard 1.4.1 fish tAs 2000 — total arsenic in fish is high but predominantly organic; the tighter inorganic control is the operative arsenic ceiling.

iAs.label: read-across from EU 2025/1891 muscle meat of fish inorganic-arsenic 100 — the toxic-species control; strictly below the total-arsenic read-across, so both are published.

tHg.label: read-across from EU 2023/915 lower-mercury fish tHg 300 — fish sauce is made from small forage fish (anchovy), which fall in the lower-mercury tier.

MeHg.label: read-across from Mexico NOM-242 other-fishery methylmercury 500 — methylmercury IS material for a marine product (aquatic methylation pathway). Reconciled against total mercury: 500 is not below the 300 total-mercury ceiling, so methylmercury is subsumed and bounded by tHg.

tomato-condiments.name: Tomato condiments (ketchup, salsa)
tomato-condiments.lineage_note: Ketchup and salsa are certified against the stricter tomato-CONCENTRATE lead and total-arsenic MLs (Pb/tAs 500, Paraguay/MERCOSUR) rather than the looser finished-ketchup (Singapore 2000) or generic-sauce (Vietnam 'Sauce' Pb 2000 / tAs 1000) MLs — a protective, government-cited choice; the finished-ketchup, generic-sauce, and canned/preserved whole-tomato MLs (Pb 50) are retained in the per-country audit trail as different product forms. Cadmium (1000) and total mercury (50) are governed by the Vietnam generic 'Sauce' category (no tomato-specific value exists — tomatoes are explicitly carved OUT of the fruiting-vegetable cadmium ML). Nickel reads across from the EU fruiting-vegetable Ni ML (400) because tomatoes are fruiting vegetables. Canned tomato condiments fall under the canned-food tin ML and are out of this bottled subcategory's scope.

iAs.rationale: No sovereign inorganic-arsenic ML exists for tomato condiments; total arsenic is governed (500, tomato concentrates). Inorganic arsenic is controlled by reflex speciation on any elevated total arsenic.
iAs.reference_method: Total As by ICP-MS; reflex iAs speciation (HPLC-ICP-MS) on any total-As exceedance.

MeHg.rationale: No methylation pathway and no fish source in a tomato condiment.

Ni.label: read-across from EU 2024/1987 fruiting-vegetables nickel 400 — tomatoes are fruiting vegetables; the source-commodity nickel ML applied at face value.
